risks.note: The Company continues to primarily cater to the automotive sector. Management flags a temporary moderation in automotive growth and, more structurally, that the Government of India's increasing push for electric vehicles poses a long-term structural shift because EVs by design require fewer conventional steel-intensive components, potentially affecting demand patterns for traditional grades of steel. Mitigation is the stated push into railways, defence, aerospace and super alloys to reduce dependency.
risks.risk: Concentration on the automotive sector, with EVs a structural threat

risks.note: Steel producers face unstable prices for iron ore, coking coal and scrap metal, which management notes often represent 60-70% of production costs and can swing dramatically on mining disruptions or export restrictions, directly impacting margins and competitiveness. The Directors' Report separately cites volatility in coking coal prices as continuing to pressure industry margins.

As one of the most energy-intensive manufacturing sectors, steel is particularly vulnerable to energy price fluctuations. Recent geopolitical conflicts and market disruptions have sent electricity and natural gas prices soaring in many regions, dramatically increasing production costs and complicating long-term investment planning for energy-intensive processes.

Persistent production overcapacity, particularly from China which produces over half the world's steel, continues to depress global prices and create market instability. The Directors' Report adds that the domestic industry witnessed increased imports particularly from China, South Korea and Japan, resulting in pricing pressure in certain product categories.
risks.risk: Global overcapacity and import-driven pricing pressure

risks.note: The steel industry faces unprecedented pressure to reduce a carbon footprint that accounts for 7-9% of global emissions. The transition requires enormous capital investment in breakthrough technologies such as hydrogen-based direct reduction, carbon capture utilisation and storage, and renewable-powered electric arc furnaces, all while maintaining cost competitiveness in a price-sensitive market.
risks.risk: Decarbonisation pressure and the capital cost of transition

risks.note: Beyond carbon emissions, steel producers face increasingly stringent regulation on water usage, air quality, waste management and land remediation, necessitating additional investment in pollution control equipment, monitoring systems and operational changes that further pressure already tight margins.

The global steel market has become increasingly fragmented through tariffs, quotas and other trade barriers, creating complex compliance requirements and market distortions. In parallel the industry continues to grapple with logistics challenges, port congestion, container shortages and regional conflicts that destabilise supply chains for both raw material procurement and finished product distribution.
risks.risk: Trade tensions, protectionism and supply chain disruption

risks.note: Management states the Company is exposed to strategic/sectoral, financial/liquidity, operational, marketing, sustainability (particularly ESG related), employee related, cyber security-information and employee dishonesty, credit, product related and natural calamity risks. The Board has constituted a Risk Management Committee to oversee identification, assessment, analysis, treatment, mitigation, control and monitoring. The volatility of the steel industry is stated to affect both financial and non-financial results of the business.
risks.risk: Broad enterprise risk set overseen by the Risk Management Committee

currentContext.expansion: Sunflag's expansion in FY 2025-26 was incremental rather than greenfield: under 'Projects — Steel Plant' the Directors' Report states only that the Company continued to keep upgrading its existing steel making facilities, focusing on new grade developments and enhancing its capability to cater to new market segments. The substantive capability addition sits in the Super Alloy manufacturing facility, which has established the capability to produce high-performance special steels for commercial and fighter aircraft, defence systems, space vehicles, nuclear reactors, power plants, industrial and aero gas turbines and petrochemical plants, and which is now capable of manufacturing plates and rings in special steel grades in addition to bars and billets, further expanding the product portfolio for strategic industries. Energy-side expansion runs through joint ventures rather than on-balance-sheet plant: ReNew Green (MPR Three) Private Limited, a JV with ReNew Green Energy Solution Pvt. Ltd. in which Sunflag holds 31.2%, is setting up a 71.34 MW Solar Photovoltaic Power Project at Village Bagapur, Yavatmal, Maharashtra; and Sunflag executed a Share Subscription and Shareholders' Agreement to hold at least 26% of Sunsure Solarpark Thirty Seven Private Limited (36.27% of its equity share capital as at 31 March 2026) to procure power from an 11.00 MW AC / 16.5 MWp DC grid-connected solar project at Ajande Kh, Taluka Sindhkeda, District Dhule, Maharashtra. Sunflag also invested a further INR 3,43,00,000 during the year in JV Ramesh Sunwire Private Limited, taking total investment to INR 13,23,00,000 for a 49% stake in that alloy steel wire venture. Two legacy projects remain stalled: the Hanol-Tuini hydro power project of wholly-owned subsidiary Sunflag Power Limited has been sub judice since 2023 with no specific developments, and the Khappa, Madanpur (North) and C T Mining coal blocks stood de-allocated following the Supreme Court order of 24 September 2014. Forward-looking, the Company continues to evaluate opportunities for securing strategic raw material resources including coal and iron ore mines to strengthen supply security and improve long-term cost competitiveness. No commissioning dates, project costs or capacity-addition tonnages are disclosed for any steel-plant project.

risks.risk: Concentration on the automotive sector, with EVs a structural threat
risks.note: The Company continues to primarily cater to the automotive sector. Management flags a temporary moderation in automotive growth and, more structurally, that the Government of India's increasing push for electric vehicles poses a long-term structural shift because EVs by design require fewer conventional steel-intensive components, potentially affecting demand patterns for traditional grades of steel. Mitigation is the stated push into railways, defence, aerospace and super alloys to reduce dependency.

Steel producers face unstable prices for iron ore, coking coal and scrap metal, which management notes often represent 60-70% of production costs and can swing dramatically on mining disruptions or export restrictions, directly impacting margins and competitiveness. The Directors' Report separately cites volatility in coking coal prices as continuing to pressure industry margins.

As one of the most energy-intensive manufacturing sectors, steel is particularly vulnerable to energy price fluctuations. Recent geopolitical conflicts and market disruptions have sent electricity and natural gas prices soaring in many regions, dramatically increasing production costs and complicating long-term investment planning for energy-intensive processes.

risks.risk: Global overcapacity and import-driven pricing pressure
risks.note: Persistent production overcapacity, particularly from China which produces over half the world's steel, continues to depress global prices and create market instability. The Directors' Report adds that the domestic industry witnessed increased imports particularly from China, South Korea and Japan, resulting in pricing pressure in certain product categories.

risks.risk: Decarbonisation pressure and the capital cost of transition
risks.note: The steel industry faces unprecedented pressure to reduce a carbon footprint that accounts for 7-9% of global emissions. The transition requires enormous capital investment in breakthrough technologies such as hydrogen-based direct reduction, carbon capture utilisation and storage, and renewable-powered electric arc furnaces, all while maintaining cost competitiveness in a price-sensitive market.

Beyond carbon emissions, steel producers face increasingly stringent regulation on water usage, air quality, waste management and land remediation, necessitating additional investment in pollution control equipment, monitoring systems and operational changes that further pressure already tight margins.

risks.risk: Trade tensions, protectionism and supply chain disruption
risks.note: The global steel market has become increasingly fragmented through tariffs, quotas and other trade barriers, creating complex compliance requirements and market distortions. In parallel the industry continues to grapple with logistics challenges, port congestion, container shortages and regional conflicts that destabilise supply chains for both raw material procurement and finished product distribution.

risks.risk: Broad enterprise risk set overseen by the Risk Management Committee
risks.note: Management states the Company is exposed to strategic/sectoral, financial/liquidity, operational, marketing, sustainability (particularly ESG related), employee related, cyber security-information and employee dishonesty, credit, product related and natural calamity risks. The Board has constituted a Risk Management Committee to oversee identification, assessment, analysis, treatment, mitigation, control and monitoring. The volatility of the steel industry is stated to affect both financial and non-financial results of the business.

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.
